text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock jumped 2.6% today to $383, continuing a sharp six-day rally that's seen it gain 7.8% since August 25. The immediate driver is escalating U.S.-Iran military tensions — oil prices spiked to $90 a barrel on fresh American strikes against Iranian targets on Tuesday, with Wednesday bringing another round of tit-for-tat strikes that pushed crude higher still. Refineries are running at 97.4% capacity, near maximum utilization, so when oil prices rise, refiners like Marathon profit from the wider spread between their input costs and output — they're essentially converting more expensive crude into fuel at favorable margins.

The move fits a broader trend: geopolitical risk in the Middle East is tightening global oil markets at a moment when U.S. refinery capacity is already maxed out. That combination amplifies refiners' advantage when crude rallies.
